advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a shim-liveness anchor (e.g. the shim logs every invocation, or assert the session-finish `status --porcelain` went through the shim) before trusting `not state.exists()` in test_real_commit_guard_reads_head_without_starting_git
evidence:
tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:148-149: `if operation == "status":
        assert int(state.read_text()) >= 2, "the shim did not block the real guard probe"` (the diff made the liveness check status-only)
tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:60-65: the shim writes state only when `args[-2:] == tail`; other git calls pass through and leave no trace, so nothing in the capture shows the shim ran
returncode == 0 shows that nested pytest passed a test. It does not show that git calls went through the shim, and it would be 0 just the same if the real git were used.
advisory.finding: test_real_commit_guard_reads_head_without_starting_git decides pass or fail from an absence (`not state.exists()`) and never shows that the git shim was reachable. The diff limited the helper's shim-liveness assertion to `operation == "status"`, so the 'head' case has no anchor. If the shim isn't on the nested process's PATH, or the nested guard never runs, the counter file is still absent and the test passes even when the guard starts git for HEAD.
scenarios: A later change to subprocess_env/_child_env drops the prepended bin_dir from PATH. The guard then calls the real `git rev-parse HEAD`, which succeeds, the state file is never written, and the test still passes while the regression it exists to catch goes unnoticed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have the shim append each invocation's args to a log file. Then assert the log is non-empty (for example, that it contains the session-finish `status --porcelain` probe) and that no entry ends with `rev-parse HEAD`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_commit_guard_fails_explicitly_when_the_head_probe_times_out, lower the timeout to 0.5 s only after the healthy first head() call (and assert state == "1" there), matching the sibling test
evidence: tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:66: persistent shim stalls when `count + 1 >= 2`, so any retry of the first call stalls
advisory.finding: test_commit_guard_fails_explicitly_when_the_head_probe_times_out sets GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to 0.5 before the healthy first call `assert _isolation.head(repo)`. On a loaded host, the Python shim plus the exec'd git can take longer than 0.5 s. The retry then increments the counter to 2, and the persistent shim stalls every later call. TimeoutExpired is then raised from the setup line, outside `pytest.raises`, and the test errors. The sibling test sets the 0.5 s bound only after its healthy call.
scenarios: Under xdist on a host at load ~40 (the scenario in the commit message), the first healthy probe takes more than 0.5 s, gets retried into the stalling shim, and the test errors with TimeoutExpired on line 274.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move `patch.setattr(_isolation, "GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 0.5)` to after `assert _isolation.head(repo)`, and add `assert state.read_text() == "1"` before it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Parametrize the deferral test over GIT_DIR/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, add a reftable-layout case (skip if git lacks --ref-format) and an annotated tag before pack-refs
evidence: No test creates an annotated tag before `pack-refs --all`, so the `line.startswith(("#", "^"))` skip is never hit on a `^` line
advisory.finding: Several deferral branches added in _read_head_from_files/_git_dirs have no tests: the reftable backend returning None, GIT_COMMON_DIR or GIT_WORK_TREE set (only GIT_DIR is tested), and a `.git` file without a `gitdir: ` prefix. The packed-refs reader is never tested with peeled `^` lines (the packed test has no annotated tag).
scenarios: A refactor drops the reftable check or one of the env names. The reader then returns a stale or wrong SHA for that layout, and no test fails.
